title: Stabilize SDK replay orchestrator and add end-to-end contract assertions
creator: Michael Chen
description: Goal: harden the SDK deterministic-replay harness and introduce a lightweight contract assertion layer that runs against the Redwood API (hosted mock + replay fixtures). This ticket covers: 1) making the orchestrator deterministic across Python/TS/Go SDKs (time-freeze, VCR-style request matching, canonical headers), 2) improving streaming ergonomics in recorded flows so replayed streams match chunking behavior produced in production, and 3) a set of end-to-end contract assertions that validate critical API surface (status codes, mandatory fields, structured output stability). The motivation is to reduce flaky CI runs and give SDK owners faster feedback when runtime or API changes cause behavior regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator reproduces previously recorded sessions deterministically for Python, TS, and Go SDKs in CI >95% of runs
VCR-style matcher supports header normalization, clock skew tolerance, and token-independent request ids
Streaming replays produce identical chunk boundaries or provide a documented and stable chunking compatibility mode for SDKs
A contract test suite runs against the hosted mock server and a small set of live Redwood endpoints; failures surface as CI gating failures with clear assertion diffs
Documentation and a runbook for capturing new fixtures, updating contracts, and marking intentional changes (opt-in schema bumps)
implementation_notes: Add deterministic time provider injection to replay harness; default to recorded timestamp but allow fixed-clock mode for CI
Implement request fingerprinting: method + path + canonicalized query + body hash + normalized headers (authorization/token redacted)
Introduce a streaming replay shim that supports two modes: precise-chunk (exact chunk boundaries) and token-stable (semantically same tokens but coalesced chunks)
Create contract assertions DSL: required_fields, field_types, and stable_enums with clear diff output
Expose a small CLI: `redwood-replay update-fixture`, `redwood-replay run-contracts --live` for maintainers
Add test hooks in Python/TS/Go SDKs to toggle replay mode and surface SDK-level ergonomic invariants (iterator behavior, async callbacks)
progress_updates: 2025-11-04 - Kickoff: aligned on scope with SDK leads (Python: Asha, TS: Daniel Rivera, Go: Priya Shah). Identified biggest flakes: streaming chunk mismatch and timestamp drift.
2025-11-06 - Prototype: clock injection added to the NodeJS replay harness; initial fingerprinting implemented; observed deterministic runs locally for 20/20 iterations.
2025-11-08 - Integration: ported canonical header logic to Python harness; discovered Go SDK uses different newline normalization for multiline string bodies (follow-up item created).

2025-11-11 - First contract draft: wrote 12 lightweight contract assertions covering generate/chat/embeddings endpoints; failing cases show structured-output field rename in a historical fixture (decided to mark as allowed backward-compat change).
decisions: Prefer a permissive default for streaming replay: token-stable mode by default to reduce churn; precise-chunk mode available behind a flag for low-level tests
Store fixtures in `infra/sdks/replay-fixtures/` with a versioned manifest and checksum to detect accidental edits
Contract test failures will be triaged by SDK owners in the first 24h; failures affecting >1 SDK escalate to Runtime oncall
Do not redact non-sensitive schema fields in contracts; only redact tokens/keys to keep diffs actionable
risks: Large recorded streams increase fixture size and slow CI; mitigation: keep heavy golden recordings gated to a nightly job and use trimmed fixtures for PR-level checks
False positives from contract tests if contracts are too strict — mitigation: implement stable_enums and opt-in schema-bump flow
Cross-language normalization edge cases (Go vs Python newline/encoding) may require per-sdk adapters
